land.text: Egypt, taken when the Bahri Mamluks overthrew the Ayyubids in 1250

predecessors.note: Only Egypt in 1250; the Syrian Ayyubid rump survived until the Mongols took it in 1260 (ayyubid-sultanate dossier). Cliopatria's 1241-1249 'Mamluk' row is that Syrian rump, not a Mamluk state.

land.text: Syria (after Marj Dabiq, 24 August 1516), Egypt (22 January 1517) and the Hejaz; Yemen only partly ('control of Yemen remained partial and sporadic')

successors.note: The Ottoman-Mamluk War page: the Levant, Egypt and Hejaz 'incorporated as provinces of the Ottoman Empire'.

capitals.name: Cairo
capitals.note: The page gives 'Cairo as its capital' throughout; Ayyubid Egypt's capital 1218-1250 was also Cairo.

correction.text: not Mamluk: the shape is unchanged but belongs to ayyubid-sultanate for 1241-1249; the Mamluk state has no land before 1250

keyframe_review.note: The page: 'The sultanate was established with the overthrow of the Ayyubid dynasty in Egypt in 1250' (infobox 'Murder of Turanshah: 2 May 1250'). The 287,000 km2 shape (Syria, Jordan, south-east Turkey, 1241-1249) is the Syrian Ayyubid principalities: by 1250 an-Nasir Yusuf held Syria 'from the Khabur River to the Sinai Peninsula, apart from Hama and Transjordan' (Ayyubid page). It belongs under the ayyubid-sultanate dossier, which adds it to its own 1241 shape.

minus.text: 1250-1259: Egypt (and the Hejaz as Cliopatria draws it), without Syria
the Hejaz, outside Egyptian suzerainty since the Rasulids took Mecca in 1238

correction.text: 1250-1259: Egypt, without Syria ; without the Hejaz

keyframe_review.note: The page gives no area. Cliopatria's 1.52 M km2 is the Ayyubid Egypt-and-Syria shape, but 'They then conquered or gained suzerainty over the Ayyubids' Syrian principalities' only after Ain Jalut (1260), and the Bahriyya and al-Mughith Umar 'twice attempted to conquer Egypt in November 1257 and 1258 but were defeated'. In 1250-1259 the Mamluks hold Egypt (and, as Cliopatria draws it, the Hejaz; the page says only that the sultanate expanded into the Hejaz 'by the end of the 13th century', so the Hejaz is a gap). fx-27: the Hejaz is subtracted from 1250-1271. The Ayyubid page: the Rasulids 'ended Ayyubid suzerainty in the Hejaz, which they completed in 1238 when Nur al-Din Umar captured Mecca'; the Mamluk Sultanate page gives no date for Mamluk control of the Hejaz before 'the end of the 13th century' (under Baybars, Qalawun and al-Ashraf Khalil) and nothing for 1250-1260. The Sharifate of Mecca keeps its Hejaz keyframe (from 1201) and data/hierarchy.csv makes it a Mamluk vassal from 1269.

minus.text: 1260-1271: Egypt, the Hejaz and Syria with Aleppo from October 1260
the Hejaz, outside Egyptian suzerainty since the Rasulids took Mecca in 1238

correction.text: 1260-1271: Egypt and Syria with Aleppo from October 1260 ; without the Hejaz

keyframe_review.note: 1.35 M km2, bbox north to 34.2 N: Egypt, the Hejaz and Damascus with the south of Syria. The shape stops short of Aleppo and the north, yet the Ain Jalut page says 'the Mamluks captured Damascus five days later after Ain Jalut, followed by Aleppo within a month' (3 September 1260) and the infobox has 'The Mongols withdraw from the Levant and cede occupied territories to the Mamluk Sultanate'; the Mongol force Hulegu sent in December 1260 came 'in his sole attempt to attack the Mamluks in Aleppo' and, after a fortnight, 'could make no other progress and had to retreat', so no other state holds Aleppo in 1260-1271. Aleppo (region), 72 cells at 36.3-38.0 E, 35.6-36.9 N, is added from October 1260 (the mongol-empire dossier ends its occupation in the same month); the union is 4,727 cells against Cliopatria's 4,655. Homs (Ayyubid emirate until 1262; ledger), Hama (vassal) and the Frankish coast stay outside. The Mamluk page ('Afterward, the Mamluks conquered Damascus and other Syrian cities') gave the earlier ok. The Mamluk page gives no area (confirmed). fx-27: the Hejaz is subtracted from 1250-1271. The Ayyubid page: the Rasulids 'ended Ayyubid suzerainty in the Hejaz, which they completed in 1238 when Nur al-Din Umar captured Mecca'; the Mamluk Sultanate page gives no date for Mamluk control of the Hejaz before 'the end of the 13th century' (under Baybars, Qalawun and al-Ashraf Khalil) and nothing for 1250-1260. The Sharifate of Mecca keeps its Hejaz keyframe (from 1201) and data/hierarchy.csv makes it a Mamluk vassal from 1269.

1.47 M km2. Against 1260 the shape adds about 436 cells: northern Syria (358), the Lebanese (26) and Israeli (21) coast and Turkey (21), i.e. Antioch (18 May 1268), Jaffa and Safed, Krak des Chevaliers (30 March 1271), the Assassin castles (1270-71) and the rest of the north of Syria beyond Aleppo. Aleppo itself is already Mamluk in the 1260 keyframe (Ain Jalut page: 'followed by Aleppo within a month' of 3 September 1260); the Mongol sentence for 1271 ('retreated back beyond the Euphrates when the Mamluk leader Baibars marched on them', Mongol invasions page) is a raid on a Mamluk city and moves no border, so the earlier 1271 gain was deleted.

correction.text: 1279-1293: Egypt, the Hejaz and Syria with Lower Nubia; Makuria is a vassal, not direct land

keyframe_review.note: 1.68 M km2: the shape adds 212,000 km2 in Sudan, the whole of Makuria (Cliopatria's Makuria shape of the 1290s is about the same area). The page: after 1276 Makuria became 'a Mamluk vassal state'; King Mashkouda had to swear fealty to Baybars, pay tribute 'beyond the Baqt' and 'transfer Lower Nubia to Baybars'. A vassal is drawn in the lighter tint, not as direct land; only Lower Nubia (Gebel Adda, Meinarti, up to Aswan) is direct. [Repair me-09-d, 2026-10-24] Re-read: the Makuria page says Mashkouda 'had to transfer Lower Nubia to Baybars' and that the Mamluks conquered Gebel Adda and Meinarti, but not that the transfer was kept; after 1365 Makuria is 'centered around the castles of Gebel Adda and Qasr Ibrim', both in Lower Nubia, and the Mamluk page says 'The conquest of Nubia was not permanent'. Lower Nubia is therefore direct Mamluk land only as a weakly supported reading for 1276-1293; Cliopatria's 1294 shape drops it, which the ledger now records as a confidence-1 loss in 1294.

1.47 M km2. Against 1279 the shape gains 9 cells (the last Frankish coast: Cliopatria's Kingdom of Jerusalem 1285 shape, 7 cells, is wholly inside once Acre fell on 18 May 1291) and loses the 740 cells of Makuria, which agrees with the vassal treatment above. Tripoli (1289) was already inside; with Acre 'Mamluk rule consequently extended across all of Syria' (Mamluk page).

1.47 M km2, unchanged. The Armenian Cilicia page: 'In 1343-1344 Cilicia was again invaded by the Mamluks, who were intent on territorial expansion'; no land is dated as kept, so the shape stands. The Hama principality was formally placed under Mamluk rule in 1341 (Ayyubid page) and is inside the shape already.
1.47 M km2, unchanged from 1344. unverified: page budget; the Mamluk page dates nothing between 1344 and 1363 (Cliopatria's shape id changes with the neighbour Marinid row, not the border).

1.475 M km2: 25 cells (about 7,000 km2) are added north of the 1352 shape (bbox north 37.4 N) and none lost. unverified: page budget; the page dates no Cilician gain before 1375 ('In 1365, a Mamluk attempt to annex Armenia' was stifled by Peter I of Cyprus' attack on Alexandria), so the land is not identified.

1.50 M km2, +29,000 km2: all of Cliopatria's last Cilician shape (107 of 107 cells of the Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia 1373) is inside. The Cilicia page's infobox: 'Sis conquered by the Egyptian Mamluks: April 13, 1375'.

1.48 M km2, -24,000 km2 against 1375: the Cilician plain leaves the shape. [Repair me-09-d, 2026-10-24] The Ramadanid page says the Mamluks did not lose the plain: after taking the rest of Cilicia in 1375 'The Mamluk Sultanate authorized Ramazan Beg's Turkmen Emirate to administer Cilicia' but 'took direct control of the towns of: Tarsus, Ayas, Sarvandikar, Sis at the four corners of Cilicia plain', and the emirate was 'a protectorate of the Mamluk Sultanate until the end of the 14th century' (infobox 1352-c.1397), de facto independent from c.1397. The plain is therefore the Ramadanids' protectorate land (lighter tint, ledger vassal_start 1385 to vassal_end c.1397), not a loss; the four garrison towns stay Mamluk but are too small for the shape. The Cilicia page ('Although the Mamluks had taken over Cilicia, they were unable to hold it') and Cliopatria (Ramadanid row from 1385) are the sources of the year; the Ramadanid page gives no year for the authorization.

correction.text: the 1407 shape used for 1402-1406: Syria, Lebanon and the north back in Mamluk hands after Timur's occupation ended in 1402

keyframe_review.note: 1.455 M km2: 89 cells leave the shape in 1402 (Syria 66, Turkey 13, Lebanon 10) and the same 89 return in 1407. The page says the opposite of a loss in 1402: 'Timur ended his occupation of Syria in 1402 to fight the Ottomans in Anatolia'; it dates no Mamluk territorial loss in 1402-1406, so the 1407 shape is used for 1402-1406. The Timurid occupation of 1400-1402 (Timur page: sacks of 1400; Mamluk page: ended 1402) is a ledger occupation, not a change of owner.
1.48 M km2, the 1385 shape restored. unverified: page budget; the Aq Qoyunlu appear as a neighbour from 1407 and the Mamluks later sacked Edessa (1429) and attacked Amid (1433).
1.48 M km2, unchanged. The Cyprus page: the Mamluks made the kingdom 'a tributary state in 1426' (infobox: tributary 1426-1489), a vassal drawn in the lighter tint and not part of this shape.

1.48 M km2, unchanged. Qaitbay (1468-1496) fights the Aq Qoyunlu near Aleppo (1472), the Dulkadirids (Shah Suwar defeated 1471) and the Ottomans (1485-1491, 'status quo ante bellum'); the border does not move. The Hejaz is held through the sharifs ('reduced the independence of the Sharifs of Mecca to a minimum', Barsbay).

correction.text: unchanged shape, 1516 only; Syria passes to the Ottomans in August 1516 (ledger loss), the state ends in January 1517

keyframe_review.note: 1.85 M km2, +374,000 km2: Yemen is added (the whole Tahirid realm: 1,616 of 1,633 cells of the Tahirid 1515 shape; the Tahirid page says 'The entire Tahirid realm fell under the Mamluks with the exception of Aden'). The shape then runs to 1518, but the Mamluk state ends on 22 January 1517 and Syria is Ottoman from Marj Dabiq (24 August 1516): 'Syria fell under the rule of the Ottomans with this single battle'. This verdict keeps the shape for 1516 only; 1517 is the next keyframe.

correction.text: 1517: Egypt, the Hejaz and Yemen, without Syria, until the fall of Cairo

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1-22 January 1517: Egypt, the Hejaz and Yemen without Syria; 'The Ottoman attack at al-Raydaniyya overwhelmed the defenders on 22 January 1517 and reached Cairo' (Mamluk page; the Ottoman-Mamluk War page says Ridaniya was fought on 24 January, infobox end 22 January). Cliopatria's Mamluk row runs to 1518.

region.text: Egypt, with Cairo as its capital

ledger.note: 1250: the Bahri Mamluks overthrow the Ayyubids in Egypt and found the Mamluk sultanate. 'The sultanate was established with the overthrow of the Ayyubid dynasty in Egypt in 1250'; infobox 'Murder of Turanshah: 2 May 1250' (the Ayyubid page says the sultan was killed 'in April 1250').

region.text: the Ayyubid principality of Hama

ledger.note: 1260: the Ayyubid princes of Hama (and Homs until 1262) keep their rule as Mamluk vassals. The Baibars page: they 'were permitted to continue their rule in exchange for their recognizing Baybars' authority as Sultan'; the Mamluk page: 'They then conquered or gained suzerainty over the Ayyubids' Syrian principalities'. Neither page dates it; the year is the start of Baibars' reign. [Repair me-09-d, 2026-10-24] Re-read: the Ayyubid page says 'Al-Mansur of Hama had fought alongside the Mamluks from the start of their conquest' and 'Hama continued to be ruled by the Ayyubid descendants of al-Muzaffar Umar'; the Baibars passage has no year and follows the 17 January 1261 rout of Sinjar's troops, so 1260/61 stays a bridge (confidence 1). The Abu al-Fida page (entered Mamluk service 1298, invested with Hama 'after twelve years') is silent on Hama's status.

region.text: Damascus and Aleppo, the Syrian cities the Mongols held in the spring of 1260

ledger.note: 1260: the Mamluks march north to meet the Mongols. 'advanced northwards to engage the Mongols at the pivotal Battle of Ain Jalut in September 1260'; the Mongols had taken Aleppo in January and Damascus on 1 March 1260 (same page). The zone is the Syrian land the two armies held in turn; the page names no boundary.

region.text: Damascus and the south of Syria, as Cliopatria's 1260 shape draws it

ledger.note: 1260: the Mamluks take Damascus after Ain Jalut. 'routed the Mongols under Kitbuqa at the Battle of Ain Jalut in September 1260'; 'Afterward, the Mamluks conquered Damascus and other Syrian cities.' Baybars assumed power in October 1260.

region.text: Aleppo, retaken by the Mamluks within a month of 3 September 1260

ledger.note: September-October 1260: the Mamluks take Aleppo. 'the Mamluks captured Damascus five days later after Ain Jalut, followed by Aleppo within a month'; infobox 'The Mongols withdraw from the Levant and cede occupied territories to the Mamluk Sultanate'. Filed under October like the mongol-empire dossier's occupation_end. [Repair me-09-d, 2026-10-24] Replaces the 1271 gain, which misread the Mongol invasions page: its 1271 sentence ('moved southwards from Rum and captured Aleppo', then 'retreated back beyond the Euphrates when ... Baibars marched on them') is a raid on a city that was already Mamluk and moves no border; the Ain Jalut page also has Hulegu's December 1260 force attacking 'the Mamluks in Aleppo' and retreating after a fortnight.

region.text: Homs, the Ayyubid principality of al-Ashraf Musa

ledger.counterpart: Ayyubid emirate of Homs (al-Ashraf Musa; no dossier)
ledger.note: 1262: Baibars annexes Homs. 'After al-Ashraf Musa's death in 1262, the new Mamluk sultan, Baibars, annexed Homs.' [Reviewer me-09-d, 2026-10-24] Counterpart changed from ayyubid-sultanate, whose dossier ends in 1260: the Ayyubid dynasty page says al-Ashraf Musa had been allowed to keep governing Homs after Hulagu's arrival, and 'After al-Ashraf Musa's death in 1262, the new Mamluk sultan, Baibars, annexed Homs.'

region.text: Kerak and Transjordan, the Ayyubid principality of al-Mughith Umar

ledger.counterpart: Ayyubid emirate of Kerak (al-Mughith Umar; no dossier)
ledger.note: c. 1263: Kerak is surrendered to Baibars. 'al-Mughith Umar was tricked into surrendering Karak to Baibars', 'the next year' after al-Ashraf Musa's death in 1262. [Reviewer me-09-d, 2026-10-24] Counterpart changed from ayyubid-sultanate, whose dossier ends in 1260: the Ayyubid dynasty page, 'The next year, al-Mughith Umar was tricked into surrendering Karak to Baibars'.

region.text: the Frankish coastal strip of the Kingdom of Jerusalem

ledger.note: 1265: Baibars begins taking the Frankish coast. 'capturing Arsuf in 1265' is the first dated place the Mamluks take from the crusaders; the campaigns of 1266-1271 follow and the zone is closed at Acre in 1291.

region.text: Arsuf

ledger.note: 1265: Arsuf falls to Baibars. 'capturing Arsuf in 1265'; the Baibars page puts Arsuf in a passage set in 1263 (21 March to 30 April).

region.text: Safed

ledger.note: 1266: Safed taken from the Templars. 'Baybars captured Safed from the Knights Templar' (the Mamluk page's 1266; the Baibars page dates the Safed siege 'In the same year' as 1263, a disagreement between pages).

region.text: Jaffa with the surrounding Frankish land

ledger.note: March 1268: Jaffa falls to Baibars. 'In 1268, the Mamluks captured Jaffa before conquering the Crusader stronghold of Antioch on 18 May.' The Baibars page has 'Jaffa fell to Baybars on 7 March after twelve hours of fighting' (the sentence carries no year of its own; the Mamluk page puts it in 1268, before the May fall of Antioch). Jaffa belonged to the Kingdom of Jerusalem, not to Antioch. [Repair me-09-d, 2026-10-24] Split from the earlier combined 'Jaffa + Antakya' gain, which named principality-of-antioch for both.

region.text: Antioch with the surrounding Frankish land

ledger.note: 18 May 1268: Antioch falls. 'In 1268, the Mamluks captured Jaffa before conquering the Crusader stronghold of Antioch on 18 May.' Antioch was the Principality of Antioch's capital; the Baibars page: 'In 1268, he besieged Antioch, capturing the city on 18 May'.

region.text: Krak des Chevaliers

ledger.note: 1271: Krak des Chevaliers surrenders. 'In 1271, Baybars captured the major Krak des Chevaliers fortress from the County of Tripoli.' The Baibars page: besieged from 30 March 1271 'after Baybars captured the smaller castles in the area'.

region.text: Masyaf, al-Ullaiqah and ar-Rusafa, the Syrian Assassin castles

ledger.note: 1270-71: the Assassin castles are taken. Baibars' forces 'seized al-'Ullaiqah and ar-Rusafa in 1271, after taking Masyaf the year before'; 'within two years Gerdkuh and all of the Assassin fortresses were held by the sultan'.

region.text: the Makurian kingdom

ledger.note: 1276: Makuria becomes a Mamluk vassal. 'Mashkouda was installed on the Makurian throne on 4 June 1276 and had to swear an oath of fealty to Baybars'; Makuria became 'a Mamluk vassal state' with regular tribute; 'In 1276, the Mamluks defeated King David of Makuria in the Battle of Dongola' (Mamluk page).

region.text: Lower Nubia, the Nile above Aswan to Gebel Adda

ledger.note: 1276: Lower Nubia is ceded, on paper. The Makuria page: Mashkouda had to 'transfer Lower Nubia to Baybars' after the Mamluks conquered Gebel Adda and Meinarti ('After conquering Gebel Adda and Meinarti it met the Nubian army at Dongola'). [Repair me-09-d, 2026-10-24] Re-read: the page does not say the transfer was kept, names no Mamluk garrison or governor, and has the Makurian court at Gebel Adda from 1365 and Makuria 'centered around the castles of Gebel Adda and Qasr Ibrim'; the Mamluk page says 'The conquest of Nubia was not permanent'. Confidence lowered from 2 to 1; the makuria dossier (af-01) has no mirror loss and should decide whether this was ever Mamluk land.

region.text: Damascus and Aleppo, the Syrian land fought over since 1260

ledger.note: 1281: the Mongols are beaten back to the Euphrates. Ilkhanid forces were 'beaten back to the Euphrates river at the Second Battle of Homs in October 1281'.

region.text: the Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia

ledger.note: 1285: Cilician Armenia pays tribute. After Qalawun's offensive the Armenians accepted 'a ten-year truce under harsh terms', with 'an annual tribute of one million dirhams'.

region.text: the County of Tripoli, Tripoli and its coast

ledger.note: 1289: Qalawun conquers Tripoli. The Acre page: Khalil's father 'conquered the County of Tripoli in 1289'. The Mamluk page dates only Marqab (May 1285).

region.text: Acre and the last Frankish coast

ledger.note: 1291: Acre falls and the Franks lose the mainland. 'By the night of 18 May, Acre was in Mamluk hands'; 'the final tower surrendered' on 28 May; 'When Acre fell, the Crusaders lost their last major stronghold of the Crusader Kingdom of Jerusalem' and 'Mamluk rule consequently extended across all of Syria' (Mamluk page).

region.text: the Frankish coastal strip of the Kingdom of Jerusalem

ledger.note: 1291: the fighting for the Frankish coast ends. The Latin kingdom 'continued to exist, theoretically, on the island of Cyprus'.

region.text: the Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia

ledger.note: 1292: Khalil invades Cilicia. 'In 1292, it was invaded by Al-Ashraf Khalil, the Mamluk sultan of Egypt'; Hromkla was sacked, 'forcing the Catholicossate to move to Sis'. The page says nothing of the tribute after the truce; the end of the vassalage is bridged from the invasion.

region.text: Lower Nubia, the Nile above Aswan to Gebel Adda

ledger.note: 1294: bridge. Cliopatria's Mamluk shape of 1294 no longer includes Nubia, and Makuria is again centred on Gebel Adda and Qasr Ibrim by 1365; no page dates when Lower Nubia left Mamluk hands. The Mamluk page: 'The conquest of Nubia was not permanent'; the Makuria page is silent on the date. The Makurian vassalage itself runs on to 1366 (vassal_end).

region.text: Syria, Damascus and the north, held in technical control by the Ilkhanids

ledger.note: 1299: the Ilkhanids take Syria. The Mongol army, 'in technical control over Syria', saw Damascus surrender 'between December 30, 1299, and January 6, 1300' with its Citadel resisting; the Mamluk page: the Ilkhanids 'routed a Mamluk army near Homs in the Battle of Wadi al-Khaznadar in 1299'. Marj al-Suffar (1303) and the 1313 invasion were repulsed.

region.text: Syria, the land of the Mamluk-Ilkhanid wars

ledger.note: 1322: peace with the Ilkhanate. The Mamluks 'concluded a peace treaty with the Ilkhanate in 1322, bringing a long-lasting end to the Mamluk-Mongol wars' (the Mongol invasions page says 'ratified in 1322/1323').

region.text: the Ayyubid principality of Hama

ledger.note: 1341: Hama is annexed. 'The Mamluks ... maintained the Ayyubid principality of Hama until deposing its last ruler in 1341'; 'Hama was formally placed under Mamluk rule' in 1341. [Repair me-09-d, 2026-10-24] Ayyubid page, between the two dates: 'The last Ayyubid ruler of Hama died in 1299' and 'Hama briefly passed through direct Mamluk suzerainty'; 'in 1310, under the patronage of the Mamluk sultan al-Nasir Muhammad, Hama was restored to the Ayyubids' under Abu al-Fida. The 1299-1310 interlude is not coded separately (suzerainty continues).

region.text: the Makurian kingdom

ledger.note: 1366: the Mamluks give up on Makuria. 'Reconquering Dongola was deemed too dangerous and the Mamluks returned to Egypt right after, in early 1366'; the Mamluk page says the tribute 'continued until the Makurian kingdom's demise in the mid-14th century'. The page dates no formal end of the vassalage; the Banu Kanz at Aswan stay on the Mamluk side until they are expelled in 1412/3, while the Makurian rump is centred on Gebel Adda and Qasr Ibrim (Lower Nubia) from 1365.

region.text: the Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia, Sis and Gaban

ledger.note: 1375: Sis falls and Cilician Armenia ends. The infobox gives 'Sis conquered by the Egyptian Mamluks: April 13, 1375'; the page speaks of the 'fall of Sis to the Mamluks' and of Gaban in 1375.
1382: the Burji Mamluks replace the Bahri line. The infobox lists 'Burji rule begins: November 1382' (Barquq); the state, its capital and its colour continue.

region.text: the Cilician plain around Adana, under the Ramadanid emirate, without the Mamluk-held towns of Tarsus, Ayas, Sarvandikar and Sis

ledger.note: c. 1385: the Cilician plain passes to the Ramadanids as a Mamluk protectorate. 'The Mamluk Sultanate authorized Ramazan Beg's Turkmen Emirate to administer Cilicia' but 'took direct control of the towns of: Tarsus, Ayas, Sarvandikar, Sis at the four corners of Cilicia plain'; the infobox has 'Protectorate of the Mamluk Sultanate (1352-c.1397)'. The page gives no year for the authorization (it follows 'In 1375, the Mamluks gained control of the remaining areas of Cilicia'); 1385 is bridged from Cliopatria, whose Mamluk shape shrinks by 24,000 km2 as the Ramadanid shape appears. [Repair me-09-d, 2026-10-24] Was a confidence-1 loss to ramadanid-emirate sourced to the Cilicia page ('they were unable to hold it'); the Ramadanid page shows a protectorate, not a loss.

region.text: the Cilician plain around Adana, under the Ramadanid emirate

ledger.note: c. 1397: the Ramadanids become de facto independent. Infobox: 'Protectorate of the Mamluk Sultanate (1352-c.1397)', 'De facto independent (c. 1397-1517)'; the body: 'a protectorate of the Mamluk Sultanate until the end of the 14th century'. The year is the page's 'c.'.

region.text: Aleppo and Damascus, sacked by Timur

ledger.note: 1400: Timur sacks Aleppo and Damascus. The Timur page's infobox lists 'Sack of Aleppo (1400)' and 'Siege of Damascus (1400)'; the text has 'Then Timur turned his attention to Syria, sacking Aleppo, and Damascus.' The Mamluk page puts the invasion in 1399 ('Barquq died in 1399 ... That year, Timur invaded Syria, sacking Aleppo and Damascus'), a year earlier; the Timur page adds that 'Before the end of 1399, Timur started a war with ... the Mamluk sultan of Egypt Nasir-ad-Din Faraj', so 1399 is the war and 1400 the first campaign that takes ground. [Repair me-09-d, 2026-10-24] Moved from 1399 to 1400 to agree with the timurid-empire dossier (/ledger/8, 1400). Neither page says Timur kept the cities; the end year is the Mamluk page's 1402 (the Timurid dossier bridges 1401 at confidence 1 and should adopt 1402).

region.text: Aleppo and Damascus

ledger.note: 1402: Timur leaves Syria. 'Timur ended his occupation of Syria in 1402 to fight the Ottomans in Anatolia, whom he deemed a more dangerous threat.' [Repair me-09-d, 2026-10-24] The timurid-empire dossier has the end in 1401 (confidence 1, page silent); the Mamluk page's 1402 is the only dated statement.

region.text: the Kingdom of Cyprus

ledger.note: 1426: Cyprus becomes a Mamluk tributary. 'The Mameluks then made the kingdom a tributary state in 1426' after the 1425-26 campaigns in which 'the island's Lusignan king, Janus, was taken captive' (Mamluk page).

region.text: the Aq Qoyunlu, Diyarbakir and the Jazira

ledger.note: 1433: the Aq Qoyunlu recognise Mamluk suzerainty. After the Mamluks sacked Edessa (1429) and attacked Amid (1433), 'The Aq Qoyonlu consequently recognized Mamluk suzerainty'; the page gives the two campaign years, not the date of the recognition.

region.text: the Beylik of Dulkadir

ledger.note: 1471: the Dulkadirids are brought under the Mamluks. 'Shah Suwar was defeated in 1471 by a Mamluk expedition'; Qaitbay 'later had Shah Suwar executed and replaced by Shah Budaq as a Mamluk vassal' (no year). Ala al-Dawla was compelled to shift his loyalty to Bayezid c. 1483-84, yet the page calls the Dulkadirids 'a Mamluk vassal' again at the Ottoman war of 1514.

region.text: the Aq Qoyunlu

ledger.note: 1472: the Aq Qoyunlu break away. They 'launched an expedition into Mamluk territory around Aleppo in 1472, but were routed by Yashbak'; the page does not state a formal renunciation.

region.text: Cilicia and the Adana plain, with the Dulkadir marches (Malatya, Elbistan)

ledger.note: 1485: the Ottoman-Mamluk war opens in Cilicia. 'In 1485 Bayezid launched a land and sea attack on the Mamluks' and Karagoz Mehmed Pasha's forces 'captured many fortresses in Cilicia'; the Dulkadir ruler Bozkurt had attacked Malatya with Ottoman backing. The page names Cilicia, Adana, Kayseri, Malatya and Elbistan; it does not name Tarsus or the Aleppo area. The Mamluk page: the Ottoman backing of the Dulkadirids 'soon triggered the start of an Ottoman-Mamluk war over the next six years'. [Repair me-09-d, 2026-10-24] Was confidence 1 with the zone bridged; the war page now dates the first ground taken (1485) and names Cilicia.

region.text: the Kingdom of Cyprus

ledger.note: 1489: Cyprus passes to Venice. The infobox gives 'Tributary state of the Mamluk Sultanate (1426-1489)'; Catherine Cornaro was 'forced to sell the island to Venice' (reign ends 26 February 1489), and 'Venice also agreed to continue the Cypriots' yearly tribute of 8,000 ducats to Cairo' (Mamluk page).

region.text: Cilicia and the Adana plain; the border at the Gulek Pass

ledger.note: May 1491: peace. A peace treaty was 'sealed in May 1491' and the border was set at the Gulek Pass, leaving the Cilician plain to the Mamluks; infobox 'Status quo ante bellum'. The Mamluk page: 'By 1491, both sides were exhausted'; 'the status quo ante bellum was reaffirmed.' The fighting between: Adana 9 February and 15 March 1486 (Mamluk wins), Agacayiri 26 August 1488 (Mamluk win), Adana fell to the Mamluks after a siege of about three months (1488-89), Kayseri siege lifted 1490.

region.text: the Tahirid realm, Tihama and the southern highlands, without Aden

ledger.note: 1516: the Mamluks take Yemen from the Tahirids. 'A second fleet was equipped in 1515, again under Husain al-Kurdi'; 'The Mamluk fleet withdrew after setting up a tributary regime in Zabid' and 'The entire Tahirid realm fell under the Mamluks with the exception of Aden'; the sultan was 'captured and beheaded near San'a on 15 May' (year not given; infobox ends the sultanate in 1517). The year is bridged from Cliopatria's shapes (Tahirid to 1515, Mamluk Yemen from 1516). [Repair me-09-d, 2026-10-24] Re-read: the page's Mamluk narrative carries only 1505 (fleet sent), 1509 (defeat off Diu) and 1515 (second fleet); there is no 1516 on it, the infobox runs 'Established: 1454', 'Disestablished: 1517', and the sultan's death on 15 May is placed in the same year as the Ottoman takeover of Egypt (22 January 1517), i.e. after the Mamluk state ended. So 1516 is Cliopatria's year (Tahirid shape to 1515, Mamluk Yemen from 1516) and the full fall of the Tahirid realm may belong to 1517; confidence stays 1.

region.text: Syria, the Levant

ledger.note: 1516: the Ottomans take Syria at Marj Dabiq. 'The Battle of Marj Dabiq (24 August) was decisive, and the Mamluk ruler Kansuh al-Ghuri was killed'; 'Syria fell under the rule of the Ottomans with this single battle' (Yaunis Khan, near Gaza, followed on 28 October).

region.text: Egypt, the Hejaz and what the Mamluks held of Yemen

ledger.note: 1517: the Ottomans take Cairo and the Mamluk sultanate ends. The infobox ends the war on 22 January 1517 ('Ottoman conquest of Cairo: 22 January 1517'); 'A few days later, the Ottomans captured and sacked Cairo', Tuman Bay was 'captured and hanged at the gate of Cairo', and the Levant, Egypt and Hejaz were incorporated 'as provinces of the Ottoman Empire'.

wars.name: Mongol invasions of the Levant (Mamluk-Ilkhanid wars)

zones.text: Syria between Damascus and the Euphrates

wars.outcome: Ain Jalut (September 1260) gave the Mamluks Damascus; the Mongols were beaten back to the Euphrates at Homs (October 1281); they held Syria in technical control in December 1299-January 1300; repulsed at Marj al-Suffar (1303) and in 1313; peace in 1322.
wars.note: The Mamluk page also gives Elbistan (1277, Baybars routs the Ilkhanids) and Wadi al-Khaznadar (1299).

wars.name: Mamluk conquest of the Crusader states
wars.outcome: Arsuf 1265, Safed 1266, Jaffa and Antioch 1268, Krak des Chevaliers 1271, Tripoli 1289, Acre 18 May 1291: 'Mamluk rule consequently extended across all of Syria'.

wars.name: Mamluk-Makurian wars
wars.outcome: 1265 raid to Dongola; the battle of Dongola in 1276 made Makuria a Mamluk vassal and gave Lower Nubia; Mamluk expeditions of the late 1280s, 1316-17 (Abdallah Barshanbu installed, killed), 1323, and 1365-66 ('the Mamluks returned to Egypt right after, in early 1366'); the Banu Kanz were expelled from Aswan in 1412/13.
wars.note: Tribute 'continued until the Makurian kingdom's demise in the mid-14th century' (Mamluk page). Repair 2026-10-24: after 1365 Makuria is centred on Gebel Adda and Qasr Ibrim (Lower Nubia), and the Mamluk page says 'The conquest of Nubia was not permanent', so the 1276 gift of Lower Nubia is a weak reading (ledger 1276 gain at confidence 1, 1294 loss bridged).

wars.name: Mamluk-Armenian Cilician wars
wars.outcome: Raids in 1266 (Sis sacked), 1275 (Tarsus taken, 'the royal palace ... burned'), 1281, 1285 (tribute), 1292 (Hromkla sacked), 1299-1300, 1343-44; Sis fell on 13 April 1375 and the kingdom ended.

wars.name: Timur's invasion of Syria
wars.outcome: Timur sacked Aleppo and Damascus and 'ended his occupation of Syria in 1402'.
wars.note: The Mamluk page's years (1399 invasion, 1402 end). Repair 2026-10-24: the Timur page dates the sacks of Aleppo and Damascus to 1400 (infobox) and says the war with the Mamluk sultan began 'before the end of 1399', so the war span 1399-1402 stands and the ledger occupation runs 1400-1402.

wars.name: Mamluk campaigns against Cyprus
wars.outcome: Barsbay's campaigns of 1425-26 captured King Janus and made Cyprus a tributary state; the tribute passed to Venice in 1489.

wars.name: Mamluk-Aq Qoyunlu conflict
wars.outcome: The Mamluks sacked Edessa (1429) and attacked Amid (1433), after which the Aq Qoyunlu recognised Mamluk suzerainty; Uzun Hasan's 1472 raid on Aleppo was routed.

wars.name: Ottoman-Mamluk War (1485-1491)

zones.text: Cilicia and the Adana plain, with the Dulkadir marches

wars.outcome: Ottoman fortresses taken in Cilicia in 1485 were lost again at Adana (9 February and 15 March 1486); the Mamluks won at Agacayiri (26 August 1488), took Adana after a three-month siege and lifted the Kayseri siege in 1490; peace in May 1491 with the border at the Gulek Pass and the status quo ante bellum.
wars.note: Repair 2026-10-24: the war page names the battlefield (Cilicia and Adana, Kayseri, Malatya, Elbistan); the earlier zone was bridged from the Mamluk page.

wars.name: Mamluk conquest of Tahirid Yemen
wars.outcome: Husain al-Kurdi's second fleet (1515) set up a tributary regime in Zabid; the whole Tahirid realm fell except Aden; the sultan was beheaded near Sanaa on 15 May.
wars.note: The year of the sultan's death is not on the page; the infobox ends the Tahirids in 1517. Re-read 2026-10-24: the page carries only 1505, 1509 and 1515 for the campaigns, and the sultan's death in the same year as the Ottoman takeover of Egypt; the war span 1515-1517 is the page's 1515 and the infobox's 1517.

wars.name: Ottoman-Mamluk War (1516-1517)
wars.outcome: Marj Dabiq (24 August 1516) gave Syria to Selim I; Yaunis Khan (28 October 1516) and Ridaniya (22/24 January 1517) gave him Egypt; the Hejaz followed.
wars.note: The page's body dates Ridaniya 24 January; its infobox 22 January.

certainty.note: No survey lines: the Syrian, Euphrates, Nubian and Arabian frontiers are approximate. The Euphrates frontier is firmer after the 1322 peace and the Cilician frontier after the 1491 status quo ante, but neither is a surveyed line. Vassals (Makuria, Cyprus, Aq Qoyunlu, Dulkadir, Cilician Armenia in 1285-92) are soft by nature.

sources.title: Timur
sources.note: Repair read: infobox 'Sack of Aleppo (1400)', 'Siege of Damascus (1400)'; 'Before the end of 1399, Timur started a war with ... the Mamluk sultan of Egypt Nasir-ad-Din Faraj'; the page does not say when Timur left Syria.

sources.title: Ottoman-Mamluk War (1485-1491)
sources.note: Repair read: Ottoman fortresses taken in Cilicia in 1485; Adana battles 9 February and 15 March 1486, Agacayiri 26 August 1488, Kayseri 1490; peace sealed in May 1491 with the border at the Gulek Pass; infobox 'Status quo ante bellum'.

sources.title: Abu al-Fida
sources.note: Repair read for the Hama principality: entered Mamluk service in 1298 and was invested with Hama after twelve years (about 1310); the page is silent on Hama's status. The URL suggested by the reviewer (Abu%27l-Fida) returned url_not_found twice; this title loaded.

notes:
Cliopatria rows to correct: (1) the 1241-1249 'Mamluk' shape (Syria, Jordan, south-east Turkey) is the Syrian Ayyubid principalities, and the Mamluk state begins in 1250: marked wrong, moved to the ayyubid-sultanate dossier; (2) the 1250-1259 shape includes Syria, which was Ayyubid until 1260: adjusted; (3) the 1279-1293 shape includes all of Makuria (212,000 km2) as direct land though Makuria was a vassal: adjusted to Lower Nubia only; (4) the row runs to 1518 but the state ends 22 January 1517 and Syria is Ottoman from 24 August 1516: adjusted, with a new 1517 keyframe; (5) Yemen appears in 1516 with the whole Tahirid shape, Aden included, though Aden held out.
Not settled: when Aleppo, Hama and the northern Syrian cities became Mamluk (Aleppo is settled by the Ain Jalut page: Mamluk from October 1260; Hama's vassal_start of 1260 is confidence 1: no page dates the arrangement); when the Hejaz became Mamluk (the page says 'by the end of the 13th century'; Cliopatria draws it from 1250, and the Ayyubid page has the Rasulids taking Mecca in 1238 'temporarily'); the year the Cilician plain passed to the Ramadanid protectorate (1385 is bridged, confidence 1; the Ramadanid page gives no year); Timur's invasion year (the Mamluk page says 1399, the Timur page dates the sacks to 1400: the ledger uses 1400);  the year of the Tahirid fall (1516 is bridged); Marqab (May 1285) and the late-1280s Nubian expeditions are not coded; Sivas (vassal in 1387, Mamluk page), Suakin and the Dahlak Islands (undated) and the Hejaz sharifs under Barsbay are not coded.
Counterparts that need dossiers: the Nizari Ismaili state (Assassins), the Ayyubid principality of Hama, the Sharifate of Mecca, the Anatolian state of Sivas.
Occupation events: the Timurid occupation of Syria is recorded here from the owner's side with counterpart timurid-empire (roles as the brief states them); the Timurid dossier should carry the mirror event.
Shared pages: the Ayyubid dynasty, Kingdom of Cyprus and Tahirid Sultanate pages were opened for the neighbouring dossiers; the Mamluk article was read three times (same page) with different questions. The fetch of 'Tahirid dynasty' opened the Persian Tahirids and was discarded.
Repair 2026-10-24 (author, after review): (1) the 1260 keyframe is now adjust, with Aleppo added from October 1260 (Ain Jalut page); the 1271 Aleppo gain is deleted as a Mongol raid and replaced by a 1260/10 gain. (2) The 1268 gain is split into Jaffa (March, kingdom-of-jerusalem) and Antakya (May, principality-of-antioch). (3) Timur's occupation starts in 1400 (Timur page), ending 1402 (Mamluk page). (4) The Cilician plain: the Ramadanid page shows a Mamluk protectorate (c.1385 to c.1397), so the confidence-1 loss became a vassal_start/vassal_end pair; Tarsus, Ayas, Sarvandikar and Sis stayed Mamluk and are not coded. (5) The 1485 war now has page-dated start (Cilicia, 1485) and end (May 1491, Gulek Pass). (6) Lower Nubia: the gain is confidence 1 and a bridged 1294 loss was added; Makuria and the Mamluk page suggest it never lasted. (7) Hama: the Abu al-Fida page is silent on Hama's status (the reviewer's URL Abu%27l-Fida failed; Abu_al-Fida loaded), so the vassal_start stays confidence 1; the Ayyubid page adds the 1299-1310 interlude. (8) Tahirid Yemen: the page carries no 1516, and puts the sultan's death in the year of the Ottoman takeover of Egypt (1517), so the gain stays confidence 1.
